Don't believe everything you read on the internet.  There *was* a recent academic paper evaluating the quality of commercial avocado oil, but [the press release](https://www.ucdavis.edu/food/news/study-finds-82-percent-avocado-oil-rancid-or-mixed-other-oils) was much more provocative than [the paper itself](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0956713520302449?via=ihub).  The paper concluded that there was a lot of variation in store-bought avocado oil.   This variation might be due to rancid oil or adulteration with cheaper oils, but could also be "natural variance of the avocado fruits \[or\] processing conditions\]".  It's basically a call for better standards and test methods.

Which is a long way of saying trust your taste buds.  Refined avocado oil isn't supposed to taste like much.  If you get a clear, clean oil that doesn't add off flavors to your cooking keep buying it.

Yes its normal to wash stuff in a prep sink. Its a very common method to wash tons of produce fast. The procedure should go as follows:

Remove all contaminates from the sink. Wash the sink with soap and warm water to remove any residue. Be sure to get every corner and nook. Rinse the area completely with warm water till all suds are gone. Take a bucket of sanitizer that's set to the right ratio (check your sanitizer for exact details.) Pour the sanitizer over the entire sink and let sit for at least a minute. Rinse one last time till all signs of sanitizer are gone.  The sink is now ready to work in. 

​

The entire process should take about 5-10 mins.

​

Judging by the photo you provided it looks like the sink is clean. Key word looks. Always sanitize.

1/2-1 t Goya Adobo if your grocery has it (seasoning in the Mexican section).   
**If** you can't find adobo, use couple dashes of garlic powder or 1/2 t fresh minced garlic.   
1 1/2 t finely chopped fresh cilantro or 1/2-1 t dried cilantro.    
1 small seeded and finely diced Serrano, can use jalapeno for less heat, or skip it for no heat at all


I add a little finely diced tomato but not necessary.

French Onion Soup - Ina Garten

https://www.foodnetwork.com/recipes/ina-garten/french-onion-soup-recipe-1916591


2 1/2 lbs onions, sliced 1/4” thick

1/2 cup of butter

2 bay leaves

1/2 cup dry sherry

1/2 cup cognac or brandy

1 1/2 cups dry white wine

8 cups beef stock

1/2 tsp white pepper

1/2 tsp dried thyme


In a large stockpot over medium high heat, sauté the onions in the butter with bay leaves (takes 40 minutes)

Deglaze the pan with sherry and cognac and simmer for 5 minutes

Add white wine and simmer for 15 minutes

Add the beef stock, pepper and thyme, bring to boil, then simmer for 20 minutes
